overview.title: What is Ryzome
overview.description: Ryzome is a visual workspace where your thoughts become connected insights. It's designed to solve the fundamental limitations of linear AI interactions by providing a 2D canvas where ideas exist as interconnected nodes.
overview.problem_statement: Traditional AI interfaces like ChatGPT and Claude force you into a linear conversation model. You constantly switch contexts and lose your flow, re-type prompts and explanations, struggle to see connections between branching ideas, and hit the limits of what chat can handle for complex thinking.
overview.solution: Ryzome reimagines AI interaction through a spatial, visual interface. Instead of a chat thread, you work on an infinite canvas where every idea becomes a node on a 2D canvas.
key_features: Visual & Spatial Interface: Every idea becomes a node on a 2D canvas. This mirrors how your mind actually works - thoughts branch naturally, connections stay visible, and everything flows.
Connected Intelligence: When you connect nodes, the AI understands the full upstream context. It can synthesize information from multiple sources rather than just responding to isolated prompts.
Agentic Core: Every node is AI-enabled. Generate content, transform ideas, synthesize insights - all while maintaining the visual context of your thinking process.
capabilities: Markdown-Enabled Nodes: Full markdown support with images, tables, code blocks, and formatting
Content Drop-In: Import PDFs, YouTube videos, images, web pages, and text with automatic node creation
Context Chains: Connect nodes to build context that AI understands and can work with
Instant Knowledge Graphs: Watch your research evolve into living, interconnected insights
overview.differentiation: Unlike static note-taking apps or linear AI chats, Ryzome creates a second brain that actually thinks with you. The spatial interface combined with context-aware AI enables new forms of knowledge work that weren't possible before.
target_users: Researchers building complex arguments and literature reviews
Writers developing interconnected narratives and ideas
Consultants synthesizing insights from multiple sources
Strategists mapping out complex problems and solutions
AI power users seeking more sophisticated interaction models

quick_start.title: Quick Start Guide
quick_start.description: Get up and running with Ryzome in just a few minutes

steps.title: Sign up
steps.description: Create your Ryzome account at ryzome.ai. No API keys or complex setup required - just sign up and you're ready to start thinking visually.

steps.title: Dashboard overview
steps.description: Once logged in, you'll see your dashboard with options to create a new canvas. Click 'Create canvas' to start your first visual workspace.

steps.title: Add a node
steps.description: Click anywhere on the canvas to create your first node. Ryzome nodes support rich markdown content including images and media, URLs and links, tables and data, code blocks, and rich formatting.

steps.title: Use AI (prompt hat)
steps.description: Hover your mouse over a node to reveal its AI prompt interface. The AI overwrites existing content - the node is both input and response. The prompt hat overwrites your node content, so duplicate the node first if you want to keep the original. Connected nodes provide context for better responses.

steps.title: Build context with connections
steps.description: Connect nodes by dragging from one node's edge to another. Only directly connected nodes count as context. A node can receive context from several connected nodes.

next_steps: Take the Onboarding Tour to explore all features
Watch Demos to see real workflows in action
Learn Keyboard Shortcuts to speed up your workflow
quick_start.pro_tip: Start with a simple research question or project outline. Add related documents, connect them, and let AI help you synthesize insights across your connected knowledge.

writing_in_nodes.title: Writing in a Node
writing_in_nodes.description: Ryzome nodes support full markdown formatting, making them powerful containers for rich content. Every node is a mini-document that can hold text, images, tables, code, and more.
supported_formats: Text Formatting: Bold text, italic text, strikethrough, inline code
Headers and Structure: Main headers, section headers, subsections, bullet points, nested lists, numbered lists
Links and References: Link text with URLs, internal links, image references
Tables: Full markdown table support with columns and rows
Code Blocks: Syntax highlighted code in multiple languages
JSON and Data: Paste JSON directly for structured data
CSV Data: Paste CSV content with automatic formatting
writing_in_nodes.ai_context_usage: When you connect nodes containing rich content to other nodes, the AI can read and understand formatted content including tables and code, reference specific sections from headers and structure, synthesize information across multiple connected markdown nodes, and maintain formatting when generating related content.
best_practices: Keep nodes focused: One main idea or topic per node works best
Use clear headers: Structure your content with descriptive headers
Format for readability: Use tables, lists, and formatting to make content scannable
writing_in_nodes.limitations: Very long nodes (10,000+ characters) may impact performance. Consider breaking large content into connected smaller nodes.

images.title: Adding Images
images.description: Images in Ryzome are powerful visual elements that can be used as standalone content or connected to other nodes for AI analysis and context.
how_to_add: Drag and drop: Drag an image file from your computer directly onto the canvas
Paste from clipboard: Copy an image and paste it directly onto the canvas using Cmd+V (Mac) or Ctrl+V (Windows)
supported_formats: PNG: Best for screenshots and graphics with transparency
JPG/JPEG: Ideal for photos and complex images
WebP: Modern format with excellent compression
ai_capabilities: Describe the image content in detail
Analyze visual elements like charts, diagrams, and infographics
Reference image content when generating related text or insights
best_practices: High resolution: Use clear, high-resolution images for better AI analysis
Descriptive connections: Add brief text description of what you want the AI to focus on
Organize visually: Group related images near each other on the canvas
File size: Keep images under 10MB for optimal performance
features: Zoom and pan: Click on image nodes to view in full detail
Resize: Drag corners to adjust canvas size
Move freely: Drag image nodes anywhere
Connect easily: Draw connections from any edge

pdfs.title: PDF Files
pdfs.description: PDF documents are powerful sources of information in Ryzome. When you import a PDF, it creates a specialized PDF reader node that can be used as rich context for AI generation.
pdfs.how_to_add: Drag a PDF file from your computer directly onto the canvas. Ryzome will create a PDF reader node that displays the document content.
features: Full document preview: Browse through all pages
Text extraction: Automatically extracts text content for AI processing
Page navigation: Jump to specific pages or sections
Zoom and scroll: View documents at comfortable reading sizes
ai_capabilities: Summarize the entire document or specific sections
Extract key insights and main points
Answer questions based on PDF content
Compare information across multiple connected PDFs
Generate content that references and builds on PDF material
best_practices: File size: Keep PDFs under 7MB for optimal processing speed
Text-based PDFs work best - scanned images may have limited text extraction
Academic papers: Excellent for research synthesis and literature reviews
Reports and documentation: Perfect for extracting key insights
Multiple PDFs: Connect several related documents to build comprehensive context
limitations: PDF files should be under ~7MB for best performance
Scanned PDFs (image-only) may have limited text extraction
Very long documents may take longer to process initially
Password-protected PDFs are not currently supported
workflows: Literature reviews: Connect multiple research papers and generate synthesis
Document analysis: Extract key points from reports and presentations
Fact checking: Use PDFs as authoritative sources
Content creation: Reference PDF material when generating new content
Research organization: Build knowledge graphs from academic papers

youtube.title: YouTube Videos
youtube.description: YouTube videos can be embedded directly in Ryzome as playable nodes. These video nodes serve as rich context sources for AI generation and analysis.
youtube.how_to_add: Copy any YouTube video URL and paste it directly onto the canvas. Ryzome will automatically create a playable video node.
features: Embedded player: Watch videos directly on your canvas
Automatic metadata: Title, description, and thumbnail extraction
Playback controls: Standard YouTube player functionality
Responsive sizing: Resize video nodes to fit your canvas layout
ai_capabilities: Analyze video content: Understand topics, themes, and key points
Extract insights: Pull out main ideas and important information
Generate summaries: Create concise overviews of video content
Answer questions: Respond based on video material
Create related content: Generate text that builds on video concepts
best_practices: Educational content: Works best with tutorials, lectures, presentations
Clear audio: Videos with clear speech provide better AI analysis
Reasonable length: Shorter videos (under 30 minutes) process faster
Public videos: Only public YouTube videos can be embedded
workflows: Research synthesis: Connect multiple related videos and generate comprehensive summaries
Learning notes: Create study guides and key takeaways
Content inspiration: Use videos as starting points for content creation
Fact extraction: Pull specific information and data points
Comparative analysis: Connect multiple videos on similar topics for AI comparison
limitations: Only public YouTube videos can be embedded
Processing time varies based on video length and content
Very long videos (2+ hours) may have extended processing times

web_pages.title: Web Pages
web_pages.description: Web page URLs can be imported directly into Ryzome to create web page nodes. These nodes capture the content of web pages and make them available as context for AI generation.
web_pages.how_to_add: Copy any web page URL and paste it directly onto the canvas. Ryzome will automatically fetch the page content and create a web page node.
supported_content: Articles and blog posts: News sites, Medium, personal blogs
Documentation: Technical docs, API references, guides
Research papers: Online publications and academic content
Product pages: Company websites, product descriptions
Social media: Public posts and threads (where accessible)
features: Content extraction: Clean text content without ads and navigation
Metadata capture: Title, description, and key information
Link preservation: Internal links and references maintained
Readable format: Content formatted for easy reading and AI processing
Source attribution: Original URL and publication information
ai_capabilities: Summarize articles: Extract key points and main arguments
Fact-check information: Use web content as authoritative sources
Compare perspectives: Analyze multiple articles on the same topic
Extract quotes: Pull relevant quotes and citations
Generate related content: Create content that builds on web sources
best_practices: Quality sources: Use reputable websites and publications
Public content: Only publicly accessible pages can be imported
Multiple sources: Connect several related web pages for comprehensive context
workflows: News analysis: Connect multiple news articles and generate balanced summaries
Research compilation: Gather sources on a topic and synthesize findings
Competitive analysis: Import competitor content and generate insights
Content inspiration: Use articles as starting points for writing
Fact verification: Reference authoritative sources in AI generations
supported_sites: News sites: CNN, BBC, Reuters, etc.
Blogs: Medium, personal blogs, company blogs
Academic sites: Research institutions, paper repositories
Reference sites: Wikipedia, encyclopedias, fact sites
limitations: Only publicly accessible web pages can be imported
Paywalled or login-required content cannot be accessed
Very large pages may take longer to process
Dynamic content (live feeds, real-time data) captures a snapshot

external_text.title: Copying in External Text
external_text.description: Pasting text into Ryzome is one of the fastest ways to get content onto your canvas. Ryzome automatically creates rich nodes that preserve formatting and structure.
how_to_add: Direct paste: Copy text from anywhere and paste directly onto canvas using Cmd+V (Mac) or Ctrl+V (Windows)
Smart formatting: Ryzome automatically detects and preserves HTML formatting, rich text, code blocks, tables, and links
Manual entry: Click anywhere on canvas to create a new node and start typing
processing: HTML to Markdown: Web content is converted to clean markdown
Formatting preservation: Bold, italic, headers, and lists are maintained
Link extraction: URLs become clickable links
Structure detection: Tables and code blocks are properly formatted
Clean output: Unnecessary styling and clutter are removed
best_practices: Clean source material: Well-formatted source text produces better results
Logical structure: Use headers and lists to organize information
Focused content: Keep each node focused on a specific topic or idea
Meaningful connections: Connect related text nodes to build comprehensive context
Edit after pasting: Clean up any formatting issues after pasting
common_sources: Web articles: News, blog posts, research articles
Documents: Word docs, Google Docs, PDFs (copy/paste)
Notes: Meeting notes, research notes, personal thoughts
Code: Programming code with syntax highlighting
Data: CSV, JSON, and structured information

publishing.title: Publishing a Canvas
publishing.description: Publishing a canvas makes it publicly viewable and shareable. Once published, anyone can view your canvas in read-only mode and clone it to their own workspace for collaboration.
prerequisites: Profile must be public: Your Ryzome profile must be set to public before you can publish any canvases
Name your canvas: Give your canvas a meaningful name. Default 'Untitled' canvases don't make good public content

steps.title: Make Your Profile Public
options: Option 1: Click user profile icon in side panel, click Edit Profile button, click Make Profile Public button
Option 2: Click Ryzome logo dropdown (top left of canvas), navigate to settings, update profile visibility to public

steps.title: Name Your Canvas
steps.description: Double-click the canvas name next to the Ryzome logo (top left), replace 'Untitled' with a meaningful name, press Enter to save

steps.title: Publish Your Canvas
steps.description: Click the Publish button in the top right. A modal will appear with publishing options: Canvas name (auto-populated), Description (add detailed description of canvas content), Tags (select relevant tags). Fill out description and tags, then click Publish to make canvas public.

steps.title: Share Your Published Canvas
steps.description: After publishing, you'll receive a shareable link: ryzome.ai/[username]/[canvas-slug]

managing_published_canvases.accessing: Go to dashboard/canvas home, click Published canvases tab, view all publicly published canvases with thumbnails and tags
managing_published_canvases.getting_share_links: Find canvas in published canvases, click menu button (three dots), select Copy Share Link, link is copied to clipboard

for_viewers: View in read-only mode: Can explore but cannot edit
See all content: Images, text, connections, and layout fully visible
Clone the canvas: Can copy it to their own workspace
Navigate freely: Zoom, pan, and explore like a regular canvas
for_owners: Update the canvas: Changes are reflected in published version
Edit publication details: Update description and tags anytime
Unpublish: Remove canvas from public view
Track engagement: See views and stars

best_practices.descriptions: Explain what your canvas covers and why it's useful, mention key insights or conclusions, include any special techniques or approaches used, keep it concise but informative (under 2000 characters)
best_practices.tags: Select 2-4 relevant tags that best describe your canvas, consider your target audience when choosing tags, use popular tags for better discoverability, don't over-tag - quality over quantity
best_practices.preparation: Ensure your canvas tells a clear story, organize nodes logically with good visual flow, include helpful context and explanations, remove any sensitive or private information

keyboard_shortcuts.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
keyboard_shortcuts.description: Master these essential keyboard shortcuts to work faster and more efficiently in Ryzome
navigation: Select multiple: Drag - Click and drag to select multiple nodes
Pan canvas: Space + Drag - Hold space and drag to move around canvas
Zoom in/out: Ctrl + Scroll - Use mouse wheel with Ctrl to zoom
Fit to screen: Ctrl + 0 - Reset zoom to fit all content
node_operations: Create node: Click - Click anywhere on canvas to create new node
Edit node: Double click - Double-click a node to start editing
Delete node: Delete - Select node(s) and press Delete
Duplicate node: Ctrl + D - Duplicate selected node(s)
editing: Undo: Ctrl + Z - Undo last action
Redo: Ctrl + Y - Redo last undone action
Copy: Ctrl + C - Copy selected node(s)
Cut: Ctrl + X - Cut selected node(s)
Paste: Ctrl + V - Paste content or nodes
Select all: Ctrl + A - Select all nodes on canvas
content_operations: Save canvas: Ctrl + S - Save current canvas (auto-saves enabled)
New canvas: Ctrl + N - Create a new canvas
Search: Ctrl + F - Search within canvas content

platform_notes.mac: Replace Ctrl with Cmd for all shortcuts
platform_notes.windows_linux: Use Ctrl as shown in shortcuts

pro_tips: Use Space + Drag for quick canvas navigation
Combine shortcuts for faster workflows (Ctrl + C → Ctrl + V → Double click)
Hold Shift while clicking to select multiple individual nodes
Box select: Click and drag on empty canvas to select multiple nodes in area

ryzome_challenge.title: Ryzome Challenge
ryzome_challenge.description: Join the social-first competition to showcase your best canvases and win from a 250,000 ARC prize pool
ryzome_challenge.overview: The Ryzome Challenge is a social-first competition where creators publish their best Ryzome canvases and compete for engagement both on-platform (stars) and off-platform (social media).
goals: Showcase Innovation: Highlight the most creative and impactful canvases
Build Community: Connect creators and foster knowledge sharing
Reward Excellence: Recognize outstanding work with substantial prizes
Drive Engagement: Encourage platform and social media interaction

participation_steps.title: Create Your Ryzome Account
participation_steps.description: Sign up at ryzome.ai if you don't already have an account

participation_steps.title: Build and Publish Your Canvas
participation_steps.description: Create your best work in Ryzome, then publish it to make it eligible. Only published canvases can be entered.

participation_steps.title: Enter the Competition
participation_steps.description: Visit ryzome.ai/challenge and click Enter Competition to submit your published canvas

participation_steps.title: Share on Social Media
participation_steps.description: Post about your canvas on social media with the #RyzomeChallenge hashtag. This is required and contributes to your social score.

participation_steps.title: Track Your Performance
participation_steps.description: Monitor your ranking and scores on the challenge dashboard

requirements: Account Required: Must have a Ryzome account and be logged in
Published Canvases Only: Only published canvases can be entered
Social Media Required: Must share canvas with #RyzomeChallenge
Submission Limits: Maximum 5 canvas entries per participant, 5 social links per submission

prizes.participation_reward: 300 Ryzome credits for all remaining participants

rules.public_posts: Social media posts must be public to count
rules.authentic_engagement: Unusual engagement patterns will be flagged for review
rules.fair_play: Manual review of top 20 entries and detection of unusual engagement patterns

supported_platforms: YouTube: Views, likes, and comments counted
Blog Posts: Custom content with engagement metrics

canvas_creation: Focus on high-quality, visually appealing canvases
Use rich content: images, videos, interactive elements
Create canvases that tell a compelling story or solve interesting problems
Polish your canvas before publishing - first impressions matter
social_media_strategy: Prioritize video content for the 1.5x multiplier
Create engaging threads with visuals for 1.2x bonus
Post across multiple platforms to maximize reach
Engage with other participants to build community
Use compelling captions that encourage interaction
platform_engagement: Share your canvas with the Ryzome community
Engage with other submissions by starring quality work
Participate in platform discussions about your canvas
Leverage your existing network to drive initial engagement
